purpose: Test whether an inference-only numerical solver reduces inherited-student sampling cost while retaining structure quality and validity.
checkpoint: Original459M EMA checkpoint; no new training or selected fine-tuned weights.
panel: Existing64 tuning families, all three existing evaluation seeds; original34 and reserved17 remain untouched.
cost_accounting: Midpoint evaluates the velocity twice per interval. CFG2 requires two network forwards per velocity evaluation. Thus midpoint8/10 use16/20 velocity evaluations and32/40 network forwards; Euler25 CFG2 uses25/50. Pair preparation, decoder and complete resident timing must also be counted.
self_conditioning: Predict the endpoint at the interval start for the midpoint call; the midpoint endpoint prediction becomes the next interval's self-condition. No formal second-order claim for the history-dependent learned model. Never evaluate the field at time1.
controls: Euler default remains unchanged. Same Gaussian and decoder noise for every setting, strict FP32, three decoder steps, sample-batch invariance checks for each length bucket and setting, complete coverage required.
quality_screen: Against fresh Euler25 CFG2, mean paired CA-lDDT difference must have95% family lower bound above-0.005 and coarse-valid fraction loss must be no more than0.01. Report every setting, including failed controls. Reference backbones are AFDB predictions, not experimental native structures.
next: Only a passing native/reference screen merits full48-protein ensemble quality/diversity and resident matched latency measurements. A nominal reduction in network evaluations is not a measured speedup.
resources: One H200,15-minute cap for the initial quality screen; keep project pending-plus-running total<=8 and deadline2026-10-02T15:00:00Z.
